children: on its financial debt restructuring, operational improvement initiatives, and recent commercial developments.

Largo signed a definitive debt-restructuring agreement with Caixa Econômica Federal on Sept. 11 as part of its broader restructuring with Brazilian bank lenders. Similar agreements with the remaining banks are expected in the near term.
The company also extended the maturity of its $6M promissory note with ARG to February 2028 from February 2027, subject to an extension fee equal to 1% of the principal amount.

Largo is also evaluating potential prepayment arrangements tied to its new copper-PGM concentrate production, higher-margin vanadium sales, and sales to electrolyte manufacturers serving the vanadium redox flow battery market. The initiatives are aimed at improving working capital efficiency and providing additional near-term liquidity.

On the operational side, the company said it is renegotiating key supplier and contractor deals and implementing additional cost-reduction measures to mitigate elevated input costs, including diesel and sulfuric acid.
The firm is also taking steps to reduce accumulated inventories by temporarily lowering mining rates and processing previously mined stockpiles.

As a result of these measures, the company currently expects 2026 vanadium production to be toward the lower end of its previously announced guidance range. Largo continues to maintain its 2026 production guidance for copper-PGM concentrate.

On the commercial front, Largo's annual contracting season is underway. The company currently expects high-purity vanadium products to represent a greater proportion of its sales mix in 2027 compared with 2026.

title: Largo advances debt restructuring, expects 2026 vanadium output at low end
